id: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi
title: Lekha Dodi

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 1
segments.he: <small>לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּ֒לָה:</small>
segments.en:
This poem was written by Rabbi Solomon Halevy Alkabetz, whose name שְׁלֹמֹה הַלֵוִי is spelled out by the first letter of each stanza. In this poem, the bridegroom (Israel) calls to his Beloved Friend (God) asking that He join him in welcoming his bride (the Sabbath). The concept of welcoming the Sabbath goes back to Talmudic times. Rabbi Chanina robed himself and stood at sunset on the eve of the Sabbath and exclaimed, “Come! Let us go forth to welcome the Sabbath Queen.” Rabbi Yanai garbed himself in festive attire on Sabbath eve and exclaimed; “Come bride, Come bride” (Shabbos 119a).
Come my Beloved Friend to greet the bride, let us welcome the Sabbath.

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 2
segments.he: שָׁמוֹר וְזָכוֹר בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד. הִשְׁמִיעָֽנוּ אֵל הַמְיוּחָד. יְהֹוָה אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד. לְשֵׁם וּלְתִפְאֶֽרֶת וְלִתְהִלָּה:
segments.en: “Preserve” and “Remember” in a single utterance the One Almighty caused us to hear; Adonoy is One, and His Name is One; for fame, for glory, and for praise.

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 3
segments.he: <small>לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּ֒לָה:</small>
segments.en: <small>Come my Beloved Friend to greet the bride, let us welcome the Sabbath.</small>

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 4
segments.he: לִקְרַאת שַׁבָּת לְכוּ וְנֵלְ֒כָה. כִּי הִיא מְקוֹר הַבְּ֒רָכָה. מֵרֹאשׁ מִקֶּֽדֶם נְסוּכָה. סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה:
segments.en: To greet the Sabbath, come let us go for it is the source of blessing; from the very beginning, of old, it was appointed; last in creation, first in [God's] thought.

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 5
segments.he: <small>לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּ֒לָה:</small>
segments.en: <small>Come my Beloved Friend to greet the bride, let us welcome the Sabbath.</small>

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 6
segments.he: מִקְדַּשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ עִיר מְלוּכָה. קֽוּמִי צְאִי מִתּוֹךְ הַהֲפֵכָה. רַב לָךְ שֶֽׁבֶת בְּעֵֽמֶק הַבָּכָא. וְהוּא יַחְמוֹל עָלַֽיִךְ חֶמְלָה:
segments.en: Sanctuary of the King, royal city, arise, come forth from the upheaval; too long have you dwelt in the valley of weeping; He will show you abundant pity.

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 7
segments.he: <small>לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּ֒לָה:</small>
segments.en: <small>Come my Beloved Friend to greet the bride, let us welcome the Sabbath.</small>

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 8
segments.he: הִתְנַעֲרִי מֵעָפָר קֽוּמִי. לִבְשִׁי בִּגְדֵי תִפְאַרְתֵּךְ עַמִּי. עַל יַד בֶּן יִשַּׁי בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי. קָרְבָה אֶל נַפְשִׁי גְּאָלָהּ:
segments.en: Shake the dust off yourself, arise, dress up in your garments of glory, my people; through the son of Yishai the Bethlehemite, draw near to my soul and redeem it.

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 9
segments.he: <small>לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּ֒לָה:</small>
segments.en: <small>Come my Beloved Friend to greet the bride, let us welcome the Sabbath.</small>

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 10
segments.he: הִתְעוֹרְ֒רִי. הִתְעוֹרְ֒רִי. כִּי בָא אוֹרֵךְ קֽוּמִי אֽוֹרִי. עֽוּרִי עֽוּרִי שִׁיר דַּבֵּֽרִי. כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה עָלַֽיִךְ נִגְלָה:
segments.en: Wake up! wake up! for your light has come, arise and shine. Awaken! awaken! utter a song, The glory of Adonoy is revealed upon you.

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 11
segments.he: <small>לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּ֒לָה:</small>
segments.en: <small>Come my Beloved Friend to greet the bride, let us welcome the Sabbath.</small>

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 12
segments.he: לֹא תֵבֽוֹשִׁי וְלֹא תִכָּלְ֒מִי. מַה תִּשְׁתּוֹחֲחִי וּמַה תֶּהֱמִי. בָּךְ יֶחֱסוּ עֲנִיֵּי עַמִּי. וְנִבְנְ֒תָה עִיר עַל תִּלָּהּ:
segments.en: Feel not ashamed or humiliated why are you bowed down, why do you moan? In you will take refuge the poor of my people; and the city will be rebuilt on its ancient site.

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 13
segments.he: <small>לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּ֒לָה:</small>
segments.en: <small>Come my Beloved Friend to greet the bride, let us welcome the Sabbath.</small>

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 14
segments.he: וְהָיוּ לִמְשִׁסָּה שֹׁסָֽיִךְ. וְרָחֲקוּ כָּל מְבַלְּ֒עָֽיִךְ. יָשִׂישׂ עָלַֽיִךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ. כִּמְשׂוֹשׂ חָתָן עַל כַּלָּה:
segments.en: They will be ravaged, those who ravaged you, and they will be cast far off, all who devour you. Your God will rejoice over you as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride.

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 15
segments.he: <small>לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּ֒לָה:</small>
segments.en: <small>Come my Beloved Friend to greet the bride, let us welcome the Sabbath.</small>

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 16
segments.he: יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל תִּפְרֽוֹצִי. וְאֶת יְהֹוָה תַּעֲרִֽיצִי. עַל יַד אִישׁ בֶּן פַּרְצִי. וְנִשְׂמְ֒חָה וְנָגִֽילָה:
segments.en: Right and left you will spread out. and Adonoy, you will praise; through the man descended from Peretz we will rejoice and exult.

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 17
segments.he: <small>לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּ֒לָה:</small>
segments.en: <small>Come my Beloved Friend to greet the bride, let us welcome the Sabbath.</small>

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 18
segments.he: בּֽוֹאִי בְשָׁלוֹם עֲטֶֽרֶת בַּעְלָהּ. גַּם בְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְצָהֳלָה. תּוֹךְ אֱמוּנֵי עַם סְגֻלָּה. בֹּֽאִי כַלָּה בֹּֽאִי כַלָּה בֹּֽאִי כַלָּה שַׁבָּת מַלְכְּתָא:
segments.en: Come in peace, crown of her husband, come rejoicing and with good cheer; amidst the faithful of the treasured people. Come Bride, come Bride, come Bride, Shabbos Queen!

segments.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Kabbalat Shabbat, Lekha Dodi 19
segments.he: <small>לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּ֒לָה:</small>
segments.en: <small>Come my Beloved Friend to greet the bride, let us welcome the Sabbath.</small>
